← All problemsThe exact dyadic denominator law in shifted Jacobi parametersLet $u=\alpha^2-	frac14$ and $v= eta^2-	frac14$ be independent indeterminates. Following Area's formal Definition 2.1, put $P_\ell(z)=\prod_{0\le j<\ell}(z-j(j+1)),\qquad C_s(\xi,\eta)=\sum_{\ell=0}^{s} rac{P_\ell(u)P_{s-\ell}(v)}{\ell!(s-\ell)!}\xi^\ell\eta^{s-\ell}.$ In the formal $Z^{-1}$-adic ring define $F(Z)=\sum_{s\ge0}C_s(\xi,\eta)\prod_{j=1}^{s}(Z-j)^{-1},\qquad L_n(\xi,\eta)=[Z^{-n}]\log F(Z),$ and $\kappa_r(u,v)=2^{-(2r-1)}\operatorname{Im}L_{2r-1}\!\left( rac{1+i}{2}, rac{1-i}{2}ight).$ Empty products are one; coefficient extraction is finite at each order, and $u,v$ are treated as real formal variables. Shifted-parameter question (Remark 3.8). For every integer $r\ge1$, is the maximum dyadic denominator exponent among the rational coefficients of $\kappa_r(u,v)$ exactly $2r+
u_2((r-1)!)?$ For a nonzero rational coefficient $c$, this exponent is $\max(0,-
u_2(c))$; zero imposes no denominator. Odd denominator factors are allowed. This is distinct from the original-variable law in $\alpha^2, eta^2$, whose exponent is $3r-1+
u_2((r-1)!)$. No analytic all-order phase-identification assertion is part of this formal question.ReferencesI. Area, Dyadic denominator bounds and a transfer principle for the phase constants of Jacobi zeros, arXiv:2608.23006v2, Definition 2.1, equations (6)–(7), and Remark 3.8. https://arxiv.org/html/2608.23006v2 For the distinct original-variable law: I.
